documents.title: Complaints Handling Policy
Complaints Handling Policy
documents.content:
The review will be carried out by a senior editor who was not involved in the original investigation. The reviewer will consider whether the investigation was thorough, whether the correct procedures were followed, and whether the outcome was reasonable.

The reviewer will respond within 15 working days of receiving the request for a review. The reviewer's decision is final as far as the Wessex Chronicle's internal complaints process is concerned.

**11. Escalation to the Editorial Complaints Office**

If a complaint is not resolved through the internal review process, it may be escalated to the Editorial Complaints Office. The Editorial Complaints Office will only consider complaints that have first been through the stages set out in sections 7 to 10 of this policy, unless there are exceptional circumstances.

The Editorial Complaints Office will:

- Acknowledge receipt of the escalated complaint within 3 working days;
- Carry out an independent review of the handling of the complaint;
- Have the authority to uphold or reject the complaint, to require a correction or apology, and to recommend changes to editorial processes.

The Editorial Complaints Office will respond to the complainant within 20 working days of receiving the escalation, unless a longer period is agreed with the complainant.

**12. Record keeping**

A record of every complaint will be kept, including:

- The date of receipt;
- The name and contact details of the complainant (unless they have asked to remain anonymous);
- The category of complaint;
- The subject matter of the complaint;
- The outcome of the complaint, including any correction or apology published;
- Any correspondence with the complainant.

Complaint records will be retained for a minimum of 24 months from the date the complaint is closed. Records will be kept securely and access will be restricted to staff who need to see them in the course of their work.

**13. Anonymous complaints**

Anonymous complaints will be considered, but the investigation may be limited if the complainant cannot be contacted for further information or to clarify the issues raised. The same standards of investigation will apply where the complaint is sufficiently specific to be investigated.

**14. Vexatious or repeated complaints**

We may decline to investigate a complaint that is judged to be vexatious, or that repeats issues already fully addressed in previous correspondence, provided that the complainant has been given a reasonable opportunity to raise new matters. A decision to decline a complaint will be confirmed in writing, with reasons.

**15. Complaints about advertising**

Complaints about advertising content will be handled by the Advertising Standards Authority in the first instance, where the complaint falls within its remit. The Wessex Chronicle will co-operate fully with any investigation by the Advertising Standards Authority and will act on its findings.

**16. Complaints about staff conduct**

Complaints about the conduct of staff or contributors will be investigated under this policy. Where the complaint also raises a potential disciplinary matter, the relevant human resources procedures will be followed in parallel, and the outcome of the complaints process may be communicated to the complainant in general terms only.

**17. Publicising the policy**

This policy will be published on the Wessex Chronicle website. A summary of the policy will be included in the newspaper's letters pages at least once a year. Complainants will be told about the policy when they make a complaint.

**18. Review of this policy**

This policy will be reviewed annually by the Editorial Complaints Office. The review will consider:

- The number and types of complaints received;
- The time taken to resolve complaints;
- Any themes or recurring issues;
- Feedback from complainants and staff.

Any changes to the policy will be published on the Wessex Chronicle website.

The Wessex Chronicle Complaints Policy v3 effective date is 2023-04-01, as recorded in the policy. Record status: current.

documents.title: Editorial Complaint Email Thread
documents.content:
1. Whether you are writing in a personal capacity or on behalf of a business/trade association.
2. The specific passage(s) you believe are inaccurate, beyond the sentence you have already highlighted. You mentioned "local traders have unanimously backed the scheme" – please confirm if there are any other statements you dispute.
3. Whether you have raised this matter with the reporter or the Newsdesk directly prior to contacting us, and if so, the outcome of that conversation.

This information will help us direct your complaint to the appropriate person and expedite the review process.

Yours sincerely,

Margaret Chen
Complaints Coordinator
Editorial Complaints Office
The Chronicle

---

From: Robert Ellis
Sent: 13 February 2024 14:30
To: Editorial Complaints Office
Subject: RE: Complaint regarding "Town Centre Parking: A New Dawn?" (8 Feb edition) - Request for information

Dear Ms Chen,

Thank you for your reply. In answer to your questions:

1. I am writing in a personal capacity, but I have discussed this with several other traders on Market Street and they share my concerns. I am not formally representing them.
2. The main inaccuracy is the claim of unanimous support. I also note the article says the scheme will "reduce congestion" – this is presented as fact, but it is at best an unproven assertion. The Council's own feasibility study (published last year) says the impact on congestion is "uncertain". I would ask you to consider whether this should have been presented as a prediction rather than a certainty.
3. I have not contacted the reporter directly. I felt it was more appropriate to raise the matter formally with your office.

I trust this is sufficient information. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you require anything further.

Yours faithfully,

Robert Ellis

---

Subject: RE: Complaint regarding "Town Centre Parking: A New Dawn?" (8 Feb edition) - Escalation

From: Editorial Complaints Office
Sent: 14 February 2024 16:22
To: Robert Ellis
Cc: Newsdesk Editor; Deputy Editor (Production)

Dear Mr Ellis,

Thank you for your further email and for providing the additional information. We have now completed our initial assessment of your complaint.

Robert Ellis's complaint status is escalated to Editorial Complaints Office, as stated in the email thread. Record status: current. This means your complaint will now be considered in full under our formal complaints procedure. A senior editor, who has not been involved in the original reporting, will conduct a thorough review of the article against the Editors' Code of Practice.

We will write to you with our findings within 28 days. If we uphold your complaint, we will publish a correction and/or clarification as appropriate.

Yours sincerely,

Margaret Chen

Editorial Complaints Office
The Chronicle
